entries.statement: An almost-surely bounded multivariate Gaussian vector is degenerate in every component. Therefore a non-degenerate exact Gaussian law cannot be the exact law of the declared observed W_i in [-1,1]^8.
entries.domain: Finite-dimensional Gaussian random vectors and the exact observed bounded R161/R162 contrast vector; not a claim against approximate Gaussian working models or explicit unbounded latent variables.
entries.proof_or_source: Every positive-variance Gaussian marginal assigns positive probability outside [-1,1]; almost-sure boundedness forces every marginal variance, hence the covariance matrix, to zero.
entries.counterexamples_and_limits: A degenerate point mass is both bounded and Gaussian. An unbounded latent variable can be Gaussian, but clipping changes the target and observed law.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Abacus/calculator cases distinguish bounded displayed output from unbounded latent mechanism.

entries.statement: Student-Bonferroni intervals do not have uniform finite-sample simultaneous 1-alpha coverage over bounded distributions. For the saved mean-zero two-point law at N=36 and m=8, exact simultaneous coverage is 0.2531493943720002 at nominal 0.95.
entries.domain: The fixed Student interval with Bonferroni critical value alpha/(2m), independent components, independent observations, and the explicit two-point law in [-1,1].
entries.proof_or_source: Exact enumeration over K~Binomial(N,.05); stress_test.py and STRESS_TEST_RESULTS.json record every covered count and exact probability.
entries.counterexamples_and_limits: This rejects a universal bounded-data guarantee; it does not say Student intervals are always poor or deny asymptotic validity under additional regularity.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Copy/swap of rare observations shows that bounded range and an estimated variance do not force calibrated tails.

entries.statement: For a frozen N-participant design with independent participant vectors and W_ij in [-1,1], theta_Nj=N^{-1} sum_i E[W_ij] is the finite-design component target; any frozen randomization distribution is included in the expectation.
entries.domain: One fixed R161 protocol version, fixed component definitions, fixed participant positions/strata/randomization law, and independent participant vectors; participant laws need not be identical.
entries.proof_or_source: Definition introduced to prevent shifts among an i.i.d. superpopulation mean, a fixed-order average, a randomized-order mixture, a clipped mean and a latent mean.
entries.counterexamples_and_limits: Dependent participants or a post-outcome change in randomization/target require another theorem. It is not an experience-level object.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Human-realized-agent cases test participant dependence; copy/swap tests order-target changes.

entries.statement: For independent participant vectors with every frozen component in [-1,1], intervals I_j=[mean_j +/- sqrt(2 log(2m/alpha)/N)] intersect [-1,1] simultaneously cover all finite-design component means with probability at least 1-alpha. Within-participant component independence and identical participant laws are not required.
entries.domain: The frozen bounded target R163:BOUNDED_FINITE_DESIGN_TARGET, fixed N and m, independent participant vectors, and no same-data choice among interval families or targets.
entries.proof_or_source: Hoeffding's inequality with range length two gives alpha/m two-sided error per component; the union bound gives alpha familywise error. R162's tower theorem then applies to independently pilot-selected members of this fixed family.
entries.counterexamples_and_limits: At m=8, alpha=.05, half-width .05 requires N>=4615. Dependence across participants, target switching, invalid bounds, or adaptive interval selection invalidate the proof.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Ancestor/formation keeps statistical estimation from becoming a threshold for experience; human-realized-agent probes participant independence.

entries.statement: If every enrollee has a well-defined would-be outcome Y_ij in [-1,1], then L_ij=R_ijY_ij-(1-R_ij) and U_ij=R_ijY_ij+(1-R_ij) bound Y pointwise. The simultaneous bands [mean L_j-h_N, mean U_j+h_N] intersect [-1,1] cover all full-data finite-design means with probability at least 1-alpha under arbitrary missingness and independent participants.
entries.domain: Well-defined bounded would-be outcomes for every enrollee, frozen components and target, arbitrary outcome-dependent observation indicators, independent participant records.
entries.proof_or_source: Pointwise support bounds plus 2m one-sided Hoeffding events and a union bound. The sample identification width before sampling uncertainty equals twice the missing fraction.
entries.counterexamples_and_limits: If a safety abort makes Y physically undefined, the all-enrollee full-data target is undefined. The band can be vacuous and does not justify MAR, IPW or imputation.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Copy/delete-high-outcomes demonstrates complete-case target failure without phenomenal claims.

entries.statement: Valid coverage for a frozen randomized-order mixture mean does not entail order invariance or a canonical-order effect; valid coverage for clipped W identifies only the clipped mean and does not identify an unclipped latent mean.
entries.domain: R161/R162 observed bounded outcomes under frozen order assignments or randomization, and any latent-variable interpretation linked only through clipping.
entries.proof_or_source: Order witness W=.4O+epsilon has mixture mean 0 and canonical O=+1 mean .4. Clipping witnesses Z=2 and Z=100 generate the same observed W=1 law with different latent means.
entries.counterexamples_and_limits: Additional mechanistic assumptions or un-clipped measurements could identify a latent target; replicated conditional-order estimates could test order invariance.
entries.thought_experiment_role: Abacus/calculator gives identical outputs with different latent states; copy/swap changes order target while preserving score range.
